s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic musculoskeletal pain and stress fractures with abnormal bone mineralization and phosphate metabolism
salient_findings: Stress fractures of the left rib, left sacrum, and left femoral neck
Intracortical lesion in the anterolateral right fibular head on gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI
key_facts: 2-year history of hip pain following low-impact falls
Initial imaging revealed stress fractures
Elevated alkaline phosphatase level of 220 U/L
Phosphorus level of 2.1 mg/dL
25-OH vitamin D level of 14.8 ng/mL
1,25[OH]2D3 level <8 pg/mL
Parathyroid hormone level of 37.9 pg/mL
FGF23 level of 1241 RU/mL
Bone densitometry showed Z-scores of −2.5 in the lumbar spine and −1.9 in the femoral neck
Octreotide scan was negative
Patient became pregnant and required adjustment of phosphate and calcitriol
Genetic evaluation for hypophosphatemic disorders was unremarkable
Family history was negative for bone disease
Patient had disabling bilateral hip, knee, and ankle pain after pregnancy
Gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI showed a 9×8-mm intracortical lesion in the anterolateral right fibular head

shortlist.label: Tumor-induced osteomalacia
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated FGF23 level and presence of an intracortical lesion on gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI

shortlist.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
shortlist.why_kept: Hypophosphatemia and elevated alkaline phosphatase level, although genetic evaluation was unremarkable

shortlist.label: Osteomalacia
shortlist.why_kept: Low phosphorus level, elevated alkaline phosphatase level, and bone pain

shortlist.label: Fibrous dysplasia
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of stress fractures and abnormal bone mineralization

raw.rationale: The patient's elevated FGF23 level, low phosphorus level, and presence of an intracortical lesion on the gallium-68 DOTATATE PET/MRI are consistent with tumor-induced osteomalacia, a rare condition caused by a tumor that produces FGF23, leading to phosphate wasting and osteomalacia.

rejected.label: X-linked hypophosphatemia
rejected.why: Genetic evaluation was unremarkable and family history was negative for bone disease, making this diagnosis less likely

rejected.label: Autosomal dominant hypophosphatemic rickets
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and laboratory results do not strongly support this diagnosis, and genetic evaluation for hypophosphatemic disorders was unremarkable

rejected.label: Osteomalacia
rejected.why: While the patient has osteomalacia, the presence of a tumor and elevated FGF23 level suggest a more specific diagnosis of tumor-induced osteomalacia

rejected.label: Fibrous dysplasia
rejected.why: The patient's presentation and imaging results do not strongly support this diagnosis, and the presence of a tumor and elevated FGF23 level are more consistent with tumor-induced osteomalacia
